title: Construction and demolition waste in the EU

current_state.value: Construction is the largest waste-generating sector in the EU: 38.4% of 2,233 million t total waste in 2022 (about 860 million t, of which 302 million t mineral C&D waste, the rest mostly soils). Treatment of non-hazardous mineral C&D waste 2022 (env_wastrt, computed): 80.3% recycled, 11.1% backfilled, 8.2% landfilled or otherwise disposed.

target.value: Official: WFD 70% recovery incl. backfilling (met). Circular Economy Action Plan 2020 promised a revision of material recovery targets for C&D waste; no revised number exists as of 2026-09. Proposed by the Commons: recycling excluding backfilling at 90%, landfill under 3%, plus material-specific targets for gypsum, insulation and concrete.

boundary: none directly; indirect: climate (CEAP cites 5 to 12% of national GHG from construction materials and works, 80% avoidable through material efficiency), land
context: Over a third of all waste in the EU comes from construction, more than 850 million tonnes a year. The 70% recovery target from 2008 was reached long ago, largely because crushed rubble counts as recovered even when it just fills a hole. A tighter, material-specific target was promised in 2020 and is still missing.
